clue.text: Meaning daughter's at fault

parts.note: D is the standard abbreviation for daughter
a rift is a geological fault line

explanation.surface: A parent trying to say their daughter is the one to blame.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Meaning' looks like a verb or a gerund, but it is the noun: the drift of an argument.
explanation.definitionFit: The drift of what someone says is its general gist or sense, a synonym for meaning as a noun.

clue.text: Torrent of abuse from a Welshman reportedly attached to a clan

indicators.note: what is reported is heard rather than seen, so the name is taken by its sound

parts.note: Dai is a common Welsh man's name, said like 'die'
a clan is a tribe or extended family group

explanation.surface: A furious rant delivered by a Welshman who belongs to some clan.
explanation.walkthrough: Dai, short for David, is the stock Welshman of crosswords; the opening of the answer is said the same way.
explanation.definitionFit: A diatribe is a bitter verbal attack, a sustained outpouring of abuse against someone.

clue.text: Attempt to follow Asian river craft

indicators.note: one piece is told to come after the other, fixing the order of the two parts

parts.note: the Indus flows through Pakistan
to try is to attempt

explanation.surface: An instruction to try sailing behind a boat on a river in Asia.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Craft' looks like a boat on the river, but it means a trade or line of manufacture.
explanation.definitionFit: A craft is a branch of skilled work or trade, and an industry is a branch of commercial production.

clue.text: The nation's obese wanting the best that there is

definitions.meaning: first meaning, taken literally: the overweight people of a country
second meaning: an idiom for the richest and choicest resources available

explanation.surface: Overweight citizens demanding the very finest food going.
explanation.walkthrough: The phrase is biblical (Genesis), meaning the richest produce; read literally it describes a country's fat people.
explanation.definitionFit: Living off the fat of the land is an idiom for enjoying the finest things available.

clue.text: One dependant on a salary, jocular type, leaves, surprisingly

parts.note: a wag is a joker

indicators.note: something that turns out surprisingly is unexpected, so these letters fall in an unexpected order

parts.note: taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A salaried employee, the office joker, unexpectedly quits.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Leaves' looks like the verb of quitting a job; it is only the letters to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: A wage slave is a jokey term for someone wholly reliant on pay from a job they cannot leave.

clue.text: Witty remark made by judicious chap

parts.note: judicious means wise or sensible
as a verb, skin that chaps cracks in the cold

explanation.surface: A clever quip coming from a sensible fellow.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Chap' poses as a noun for a man; it is the verb, as with chapped lips.
explanation.definitionFit: A wisecrack is a smart, joking comment, so it is a quip or witty remark.

clue.text: Flash Gordon left Earth with Arden, initially heading for Mongo

indicators.note: initially points to the opening of each word in the list before it

parts.note: start of Gordon

indicators.note: the heading of a word is its front, so only its start is used

parts.note: start of left
start of Earth
start of Arden
start of Mongo

explanation.surface: A plot summary of Flash Gordon, who leaves Earth with Dale Arden bound for the planet Mongo.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flash' is not the hero's first name here but the definition, a brief burst of light.
explanation.definitionFit: A gleam is a brief bright glint of light, which is what a flash is.

clue.text: British writer in mag housemaster put out before end of term

indicators.note: to be put out is to be disturbed, so the words are thrown out of order

parts.note: taken as written, to be rearranged

indicators.note: the end of a word is its final letter, which alone is kept

parts.note: the final letter of term

explanation.surface: A school housemaster, upset by something in a magazine, at the close of term.
explanation.definitionFit: Somerset Maugham was an English novelist and playwright, author of Of Human Bondage.

clue.text: The force of the sea years ago

definitions.text: The force of the sea years ago

parts.note: surface reading: the power of waves and tides

parts.words: The force of the sea years ago
parts.note: setter's reading: a naval force from history, the Spanish fleet of 1588

explanation.walkthrough: 'Force' reads as physical power of the ocean; it is a military force, a fleet sent by sea long ago.
explanation.definitionFit: An armada is a great fleet of warships, most famously the Spanish one of 1588 sent against England.

clue.text: Former commander extremely terse over missile

parts.note: ex- means former
OC is Officer Commanding

indicators.note: extremely points to the extremes of the word, its two ends

parts.note: the first and last letters of terse

explanation.surface: A retired commanding officer being very curt about a weapon.
explanation.definitionFit: The Exocet is a French-built anti-ship missile, well known from the Falklands War.

clue.text: Recipient of letter badly dreads getting notice

indicators.note: something done badly is botched, so these letters come out jumbled

parts.note: taken as written, to be rearranged
to notice is to see

explanation.surface: Someone who fears the post because a letter may bring a formal notice.
explanation.definitionFit: An addressee is the person a letter is directed to, its intended receiver.

clue.text: Dance with voodoo priestess

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a Latin American ballroom dance from Cuba
second meaning: the Haitian title for a female voodoo priest

explanation.surface: Dancing alongside a voodoo priestess at a ritual.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both a Cuban ballroom dance and, in Haitian vodou, a woman who leads rites.

clue.text: Member of religious group sitting in orchestra stalls

indicators.note: sitting in means seated inside the words that follow, spanning them

parts.note: the end of orchestra joined to the start of stalls

explanation.surface: A worshipper sitting in the stalls at a concert.
explanation.definitionFit: A Rasta is a follower of Rastafarianism, a faith that began in Jamaica in the 1930s.

clue.text: Cold fictional place in English city

parts.note: C for cold, as on a tap
Ambridge is the village in The Archers, a long-running BBC radio soap

explanation.surface: A chilly imaginary place found somewhere in England.
explanation.walkthrough: Ambridge is the setting of The Archers, a BBC radio serial about rural English life.
explanation.definitionFit: Cambridge is a university city in eastern England.

clue.text: Film in wardrobe I developed

indicators.note: film is developed into a picture, so these letters are processed into a new shape

parts.note: taken as written, part of the letters to rearrange
taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A roll of film kept in a wardrobe that the speaker has developed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' looks like a link word, but it is fodder too: in, wardrobe and I together give all eleven letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Bird on a Wire is a 1990 action comedy starring Mel Gibson and Goldie Hawn.

clue.text: Came into the diner, in disguise, about one

indicators.note: about means going around, so the rearranged letters surround the next piece
a disguise changes appearance, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written, to be rearranged
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Someone walked into a restaurant in disguise at around one o'clock.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Came into' reads as entering the diner, but it means received by bequest.
explanation.definitionFit: To come into money or property is to receive it by will, which is to have inherited it.

clue.text: Winning, master swimming against the current

parts.note: a team that is up is ahead or winning

indicators.note: swimming suggests something moving and swirling, so its letters drift into a new order

parts.note: taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A champion swimmer winning a race by swimming against the tide.
explanation.definitionFit: Going upstream means travelling toward a river's source, in the opposite direction to its flow.

clue.text: Ignored by old-fashioned duke

parts.note: taken as written
passé means out of date
D is the abbreviation for duke

explanation.surface: A dated aristocrat being snubbed in society.
explanation.walkthrough: 'by' looks like a link word, but it supplies the opening letters exactly as written.
explanation.definitionFit: To bypass something is to go round it or leave it out, so bypassed means passed over and ignored.

clue.text: Accept father's keeping house on variable nett earnings

parts.note: to accept is to take
a house is a home
pa is an informal word for father
in algebra, x and y are the usual variables

explanation.surface: A father who keeps house accepts living on a fluctuating income.
explanation.walkthrough: The pieces simply follow one another; 'keeping' and 'on' only join them, and the father comes after the house despite the clue order.
explanation.definitionFit: Take-home pay is the wage left after tax and deductions, the net sum actually received.

clue.text: Fine tanks seen in the cinema

parts.note: F for fine, as on pencil leads
as a verb, to tank an opponent is to beat or lick them

explanation.surface: Good-quality military tanks appearing in a war film.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tanks' looks like the armoured vehicles, but it is the slang verb for thrashing an opponent.
explanation.definitionFit: The flicks is old-fashioned British slang for the cinema, from the flickering of early film.

clue.text: Perfect surface texture

definitions.meaning: first meaning: as a verb, to complete or polish something off
second meaning: the final coating or texture given to a surface

explanation.walkthrough: 'Perfect' reads as an adjective praising the texture; it is the verb meaning to complete.
explanation.definitionFit: To finish work is to complete and refine it, and a finish is the coating or surface quality of a material.

clue.text: Queen's favourite English city?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: Robert Dudley, Earl of this title, close favourite of Elizabeth I
second meaning: a city in the East Midlands

explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that the city is also the earldom of Robert Dudley, Elizabeth I's favourite courtier.
explanation.definitionFit: Robert Dudley, Earl of Leicester, was Elizabeth I's favourite; Leicester is also a city in the English Midlands.

clue.text: Language used by male in the rear

indicators.note: in places one piece inside the other, enclosed by it

parts.note: the tail is the rear end
M is the abbreviation for male

explanation.surface: A tongue spoken by a man at the back of a group.
explanation.definitionFit: Tamil is a Dravidian language of southern India and Sri Lanka.

clue.text: Extremist drowned in awful tragedy

indicators.note: drowned in means submerged within the following words, out of sight

parts.note: the end of awful joined to the start of tragedy

explanation.surface: A fanatic who drowned in a terrible disaster.
explanation.definitionFit: An ultra is someone holding extreme views, especially in politics.

clue.text: What may tea be passed round in?

definitions.text: What may tea be passed round in?

indicators.note: passed round means wrapped around, so one piece encircles the other

parts.note: cha is slang for tea
taken as written

explanation.surface: A question about what cups tea is handed round in.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole question is the definition: fine porcelain cups, in which tea is served round.
explanation.definitionFit: China is fine porcelain, the traditional material for teacups and teapots.

clue.text: Incomparable in game against minor

parts.note: a match is a game
minor means smaller or lesser

explanation.surface: Unbeatable in a game against a youngster.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Minor' looks like a child opponent, but it means lesser.
explanation.definitionFit: Something matchless has no equal, so it cannot be compared with anything.

clue.text: He'd put in cryptic clues last in crossword, as arranged

indicators.note: put in means inserted, so one piece goes inside the other
cryptic means puzzling, so these letters are scrambled

parts.note: taken as written, to be rearranged
taken as written, apostrophe dropped

indicators.note: the last in a word is its final letter, which alone is kept

parts.note: the final letter of crossword

explanation.surface: A setter fitting cryptic clues into a crossword according to plan.
explanation.definitionFit: Something scheduled has been arranged in advance for a set time.

clue.text: Took off in one in Malta — which sea's it in?

parts.note: M is Malta's international vehicle code
I is the Roman numeral one
Malta lies in the Mediterranean, shortened to Med

explanation.surface: A puzzled traveller who took off for Malta wondering which sea it lies in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Took off' looks like departing, but it means imitated. The one goes after Malta's letter, and the question supplies the sea.
explanation.definitionFit: To take someone off is to mimic them, so took off means imitated, as a mime does.
